section_path: Studio > My Creations > Edit > Mechanics Module > Mechanics Compatibility Baseline > Frozen fixtures
control_label: Frozen fixture selector (per-fixture button, one per fixture.label, e.g. Current Empty Module, Tracker Module, Command Module, Progression Module, Status and Guard Module, Full Mixed-Domain Module, Legacy Partial Alias Shape, Malformed but Recoverable Shape, Preset-Derived Resource Loop)
default_value: First fixture in the frozen inventory list is selected by default: current.empty.v1 (Current Empty Module), set via useState(fixtures[0]?.id || "") in the view model
saves_via: NOTHING CONSUMES IT beyond local React state. The button onClick fires onSelectFixture(fixture.id), which the view model wires directly to setSelectedFixtureId (a plain useState setter). No save, submit, or persistence call is invoked anywhere in the traced chain, and the README explicitly states this package does not edit or persist a Mechanics Module and the dev preview is read-only.
handler_name: onSelectFixture (prop, wired to setSelectedFixtureId in useMechanicsCompatibilityBaselineViewModel.js); inline handler in view is () => onSelectFixture(fixture.id)
data_source: listMechanicsM0Fixtures() from mechanicsCompatibilityBaseline.fixtures.js (a static, frozen, in-memory fixture inventory, deep-cloned on each call), no network or client/service call
visible_when: ALWAYS (this whole unit is a development-only preview package; the README and the diagnostics test both note the /dev/ui-preview route it lives behind returns notFound() when process.env.NODE_ENV === production, so in a production build the page hosting this control is unreachable, but within the component itself the control renders unconditionally for every entry in the fixtures array)
notes: This is a repeatable list of identical buttons, one per fixture in the fixtures array (9 fixtures in mechanicsCompatibilityBaseline.fixtures.js), emitted as a single row per instructions. Selecting a fixture only changes which fixture's JSON, classification, and domain tags are displayed in the adjacent Selected fixture panel (also in the same view file); it has no write effect. Everything else rendered in MechanicsCompatibilityBaseline.view.jsx (contract/status/module/instance-contract summary cards, external repositories list, deferred cross-tier gates list, selected-fixture JSON preview, domain tag chips) is static display output with no onClick/onChange handlers and is not a control.

section_path: Studio > My Creations > Edit > Mechanics Module > Mechanics Json Editor
validation: Full Mechanics contract validation via validateMechanicsJsonText / validateMechanicsModuleData in mechanicsJsonEditor.validation.js (2918 lines, fully read). Requires the parsed JSON to be an object with an instanceData object plus a finite root priority and a tags array of strings. Within instanceData it enforces array types and unique ids for trackers, commands, guards, statusBlocks, and defaults. Trackers require finite min and max with min less than or equal to max and an initial value inside that range. Commands are deeply validated: unique argument names, enum types require options, NUMBER args need finite min less than or equal to max, effects require a valid effect type, id, target binding, and value binding rules including a non-zero divisor. Resolution requires a valid mode (NO_ROLL_DETERMINISTIC, THRESHOLD_DIE, OPPOSED_DIE), die count 1 to 20 and sides 2 to 1000, a threshold target number where applicable, and degree-of-success margins (critical at least 1, fumble at most -1). Requirements enforce known type and operator plus progression-specific rules. Composition steps validate phase, failure policy, backward-only dependencies, at most 3 domain steps, one domain step per patch lane, and that location actions come last. Progression profiles validate version, mode, curve type, rank ordering, and table monotonicity. Invalid JSON syntax returns a root path error. Disabled (canApply false) when jsonText is empty or whitespace only, regardless of validity.
